rules_a_to_k.how: The salivary glands are named organs, not ill-defined regions. A face or neck tumour reaches this tree only after the router's site capture names a salivary gland.

sg_histology Lymphoma option reason: a lymphoma in an intraparotid lymph node takes a lymph node site, a lymphoma of the gland takes the gland's site; Group II codes it.

sg_sialoblastoma (the report calls it malignant: 8974/3, Group XII); sg_not_malignant (intraductal carcinoma with invasion stated: 8500/3); every exclusion reason names the code with its non-malignant behaviour. Codes whose WHO term ICD-O-3.2 does not print (acinic cell carcinoma, salivary duct carcinoma, hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma, microsecretory and sclerosing microcystic adenocarcinoma) take the code with behaviour 3, and the reason names the preferred term.
No screen offers two grades: grade does not change any code here and the sixth digit is not built. The sg_histology hint says the grade does not change the code.

Salivary duct carcinoma picker reason: 8500/3 is recorded at the salivary site although ICD-O ties the term to breast. sg_site minor salivary gland option reason: a minor salivary gland tumour takes the site where the gland lies, or C06.9 when none is named.
Every term on these screens reaches its code through ICD-O-3.2 or the WHO table without reordering word roots.

sg_carcinoma_picker hint: two carcinoma types for one tumour with no entry covering both take the higher code number. sg_histology hint: high grade transformation keeps the carcinoma type's code (8550 is higher than 8020 Dedifferentiated carcinoma). conflicts.issue: The WHO lists myoepithelial carcinoma and carcinosarcoma as salivary carcinomas, but ICCC-2017 places 8982, 8980 and 8940 in XIIa4 at every site, so the tree refers them to Group XII.
Sialoblastoma is /1 in ICD-O-3.2 and in the WHO table, outside every ICCC group; ICCC-2017 holds 8974/3 in XIIa4. A sialoblastoma the report calls malignant goes to Group XII.
ICCC-2017 places 8000/3 at C07-C08 in XIIb, so a registration without tissue (basis 1 or 2) or a cytology report that says only 'malignant' is computed to Group XII, not XIf1.
ICCC-2017 holds 8407 only in XIe (C44). At C07-C08 it lies in no range, so the subgroup computation from site must place it in XIf1 under the 1 October 2026 ruling, or it returns no subgroup.
Lymphoma of the salivary gland is Group II (IIb2 for 9699 and 9680, IIa for 9650 at C07-C08). A lymphoma in an intraparotid lymph node takes a lymph node site under Rule D.
Rhabdomyosarcoma at C07-C08 is IXa; an extraosseous Ewing sarcoma (9364) there is IXd2, Group IX not Group VIII.
Melanoma at C07-C08 is XId and goes to the melanoma tree; a melanoma deposit in a parotid lymph node goes to the deposit option.
A minor salivary gland carcinoma is coded at the site of the gland: XIf10 for the mouth and other head and neck mucosa, XIc for the nasopharynx. The sg_site option re-sites it.

data_gaps.need: Paediatric occurrence of the salivary carcinomas still in the picker: microsecretory adenocarcinoma, hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma, basal cell adenocarcinoma, salivary duct carcinoma, epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma, mucinous adenocarcinoma, sclerosing microcystic adenocarcinoma, sebaceous adenocarcinoma, lymphoepithelial carcinoma, primary squamous cell carcinoma, oncocytic carcinoma, poorly differentiated carcinoma, small cell and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, and NUT carcinoma at a salivary site
data_gaps.why: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 names only mucoepidermoid, acinic cell, secretory and adenoid cystic carcinoma, polymorphous adenocarcinoma and sialoblastoma among the malignant salivary gland tumours of children, and states that carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma has not been reported in them. Pfister 2022 names NUT carcinoma in children without a salivary site and none of the other entities listed here, so each stays in the picker.
data_gaps.candidate_source: A paediatric series of salivary gland carcinoma that reports every histological type, such as the 203-case series of Quixabeira et al. that Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 cites; or WHO Classification of Paediatric Tumours, 5th edition (2022), salivary gland chapter

data_gaps.need: A paediatric case count for adenoid cystic carcinoma and polymorphous adenocarcinoma, and their order on the histology screen
data_gaps.why: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 says only that both are observed less frequently in paediatric patients than in adults, and its children's column in Table 1 lists mucoepidermoid, acinic cell and secretory carcinoma alone. The tree makes both options on that sentence and places adenoid cystic carcinoma before polymorphous adenocarcinoma without a paediatric source for the order. The controller decides whether one comparative sentence is enough for an option.
data_gaps.candidate_source: The series of Quixabeira et al. or the earlier systematic review of 2,937 paediatric cases, both cited by Perez-de-Oliveira 2025

data_gaps.need: What the WHO 5th edition salivary chapter calls cystadenocarcinoma (8440/3) and papillary cystadenocarcinoma (8450/3) now
data_gaps.why: Every ICD-O-3.2 /3 term on both codes is [obs]; the ICCR Table 1 omits them and names no successor, so a report using either term has no current entry.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Classification of Head and Neck Tumours, 5th edition, salivary gland chapter (entity list with ICD-O codes)

data_gaps.need: The Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology categories
data_gaps.why: Both sources recommend the Milan system but print none of its categories, so the cytology screen's wording for suspicious, atypical and uncertain-malignant-potential results is not sourced.
data_gaps.candidate_source: Faquin WC, Rossi ED, editors. The Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology, 2nd edition (2023)

data_gaps.need: Which gene results the WHO counts as entity-defining for basis of diagnosis 8
